table_title: List the 20 standard proteinogenic amino acids encoded by the standard genetic code, with their three-letter code, one-letter code, side-chain class, and whether each is essential in humans.
db_analog: SELECT amino_acid, three_letter_code, one_letter_code, side_chain_class, essential_in_humans FROM standard_proteinogenic_amino_acids ORDER BY amino_acid
temporal_note: The 20 standard proteinogenic amino acids encoded by the standard genetic code are a fixed, stable scientific universe; the set, IUPAC codes, side-chain classes, and human-essentiality status do not change over time. Wikipedia pages accessed 2026-05-28. Expected cardinality is exactly 20 rows. Selenocysteine (the 21st) and pyrrolysine (the 22nd) are intentionally excluded because they are inserted by recoded stop codons, not by the standard genetic code.
_extraction_notes: The row universe is the closed, authoritative set of the 20 standard proteinogenic amino acids encoded by the standard genetic code, taken from Wikipedia's 'Proteinogenic amino acid' article (selenocysteine and pyrrolysine excluded, as they are not encoded by the standard codon table). Three-letter and one-letter codes are the IUPAC standard codes listed on the same article. Side-Chain Class uses the standard five-category biochemical grouping (nonpolar aliphatic / aromatic / polar uncharged / positively charged (basic) / negatively charged (acidic)), cross-checked against the discrete charged and polar-uncharged groupings on the 'Amino acid' article (acidic = Asp, Glu; basic = Arg, Lys, His; polar uncharged includes Ser, Thr, Asn, Gln); see curation.json::normalization_decisions for the handling of the scheme-dependent cases (Tyr, Gly, Cys, Met, Pro). Essential in Humans uses the three-way human classification from the 'Essential amino acid' article: 9 essential (His, Ile, Leu, Lys, Met, Phe, Thr, Trp, Val), 6 conditionally essential (Arg, Cys, Gln, Gly, Pro, Tyr), and the remaining 5 of the standard 20 nonessential (Ala, Asn, Asp, Glu, Ser). No rows were generated from parametric knowledge; every cell traces to one of the three cited articles. Rows are sorted alphabetically by amino acid name.
